q: Which HTTP headers authenticate a request to a VTEX API with an application key?
o: `X-VTEX-API-AppKey`
`X-VTEX-API-AppToken`
`Authorization: Bearer {appToken}`
`X-VTEX-AppSecret`
`X-VTEX-Account`
`X-VTEX-API-Key`
e: Para **appKey + appToken** idzie w dwóch nagłówkach: `X-VTEX-API-AppKey` i `X-VTEX-API-AppToken`.

q: What defines which API resources an application key is allowed to access?
o: The License Manager roles associated with the key
The trade policy the key was created in
The IP allowlist configured in the Catalog
The expiration date of the appToken
The account name used in the request URL
The Admin user profile that originally created the key
e: Uprawnienia klucza to **role License Managera**. Rola składa się z resources.

q: A storefront (browser) script must call a VTEX API on behalf of the logged-in shopper. What is the recommended authentication?
o: The user token from the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie
An application key embedded in the JavaScript bundle
An application key stored in `localStorage`
No authentication, because `/pvt/` routes accept shoppers
The appKey and appToken sent as URL query parameters
The appToken wrapped in a signed JWT created in the browser
e: **Nigdy appKey po stronie klienta.** Frontend używa **user tokena**, integracje backendowe używają appKey/appToken.

q: Which statements about a VTEX ID user token are correct?
o: It can authenticate API requests for 24 hours after creation
In webstore sessions its cookie is `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}`
It stays valid until the account's appToken is renewed by an admin
It must be sent in the `X-VTEX-API-AppToken` request header
It is valid for 7 days and is renewed on every request
It works on the host of any VTEX account where the same user email is registered
e: User token działa **24 godziny** od utworzenia. Wysyłasz go jako cookie: dla sesji sklepu `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}`, dla Admina samo `VtexIdclientAutCookie`.

q: A request carries a valid appKey/appToken, but the key has no role containing the resource required by the endpoint. Which statements are correct?
o: The API responds with `403 Forbidden`
The fix is to review the License Manager roles associated with the key
The API responds with `401 Unauthorized`
Generating a new appToken for the same key solves it
The API responds with `404 Not Found`
The API responds with `429 Too Many Requests` until the key quota is reset
e: **401** to brak albo błędne dane uwierzytelniające. **403** to poprawne dane, ale brak uprawnienia. Naprawa: rola z właściwym resource w **License Managerze**. Nowy token niczego nie zmienia.

q: An integration starts receiving `429 Too Many Requests`. What is the recommended behavior?
o: Stop sending requests and retry after a backoff interval
Retry immediately in parallel to drain the queue
Switch to a second application key to keep the rate
Ignore it, because throttled requests are still processed
Lower the timeout so that throttled requests fail faster
Keep the same rate, because VTEX queues throttled requests for later
e: 429 to throttling. **Przestań wysyłać, odczekaj i zmniejsz tempo.** Orders zaleca ok. 1 minuty, Pricing podaje czas w `Retry-After`.

q: How are the authentication header names treated by VTEX APIs?
o: They are case-insensitive
They must be sent in lowercase only
They must match the documented casing exactly
They are case-sensitive only on `/pvt/` routes
They must be sent in uppercase only
They must be sent in camelCase, as in the API Reference
e: Nazwy nagłówków HTTP są **case-insensitive**. `x-vtex-api-appkey` działa tak samo jak `X-VTEX-API-AppKey`.

q: Which practices does VTEX recommend for API keys?
o: Create an individual key for each function and integration
Restrict each key's access to what its function needs
Never use API keys in client-side (browser) code
Reuse one high-privilege key across every integration
Store the key in `localStorage` so the storefront can call private routes
Share one key between staging and production to simplify rotation
e: Zalecenia: **osobny klucz na integrację**, **minimalne uprawnienia**, okresowa rotacja (przypomnienia co 3 lub 6 miesięcy) i **nigdy w kodzie przeglądarki**.

q: What does `/pvt/` in a VTEX endpoint path indicate, compared with `/pub/`?
o: The route is private and requires authentication
The route is only available inside the Admin panel
The route only accepts `GET` requests
The route is served from a separate private host
The route is deprecated and kept for legacy integrations
The route returns cached data from a private CDN
e: `/pvt/` to trasa **prywatna, wymaga uwierzytelnienia**. `/pub/` to trasa publiczna.

q: Which is the standard base URL pattern for most VTEX REST APIs?
o: `https://{accountName}.{environment}.com.br/api/...`
`https://api.vtex.com/{environment}/{accountName}/...`
`https://{environment}.vtex.io/{accountName}/api/...`
`https://{accountName}.myvtex.com/{environment}/...`
`https://{environment}.{accountName}.com.br/api/...`
`https://portal.vtex.com.br/{accountName}/api/...`
e: Standard: `{accountName}.{environment}.com.br`, zwykle `vtexcommercestable`. **Wyjątki:** Pricing (`api.vtex.com/{account}/pricing`) i Payments (`{account}.vtexpayments.com.br`).

q: A token is generated with the VTEX ID endpoint `POST /api/vtexid/apptoken/login`. Which statements are correct?
o: Its permissions are the same as those of the API key used to generate it
It authenticates requests when sent in a header named `VtexIdclientAutCookie`
It carries the permissions of the store owner user
It has shopper-level permissions only
It has no permissions until a role is attached to the token itself
It never expires while the application key used to generate it stays active and unchanged
e: Ten token jest powiązany z **kluczem API**, nie z użytkownikiem, i ma **te same uprawnienia co klucz**. Wysyłasz go w nagłówku `VtexIdclientAutCookie`.

q: What is the correct order to integrate a catalog through the API?
o: Categories → specification fields → brands → products → SKUs → product/SKU specifications
Brands → products → SKUs → categories → specification fields → product/SKU specifications
Products → SKUs → categories → brands → specification fields → product/SKU specifications
SKUs → products → brands → categories → specification fields → product/SKU specifications
Specification fields → categories → brands → products → SKUs → product/SKU specifications
Categories → products → SKUs → brands → specification fields → product/SKU specifications
e: Kolejność: **kategorie → pola specyfikacji → marki → produkty → SKU → wartości specyfikacji**. Rekordy zależą od siebie.

q: Which conditions must be met for a product to be made available in the store?
o: It is part of a brand
It is part of a category
It has at least one active SKU
It has a fixed price in every price table
It has at least three SKUs
It is linked to at least one collection
e: Produkt musi mieć **markę, kategorię i co najmniej jeden aktywny SKU**.

q: What happens when the Create SKU request is sent with `IsActive: true`?
o: The API returns `400 Bad Request`
The SKU is created and activated immediately
The SKU is created active but hidden from search
The API returns `409 Conflict`
The API returns `403 Forbidden`
The SKU is created inactive and the flag is ignored
e: SKU tworzysz zawsze **nieaktywny** (`IsActive: false`). Aktywacja dopiero po spełnieniu wymagań.

q: Which of these are prerequisites for ACTIVATING an SKU?
o: At least one image associated with the SKU
At least one alternate ID: `RefId` or `EAN`
A base price registered in Pricing
Stock in at least one warehouse
A shipping policy that covers the SKU
A list price higher than the selling price in Pricing
e: Aktywacja wymaga **`RefId` lub `EAN` oraz obrazka**. **Cena i stock** są potrzebne do widoczności w sklepie, nie do aktywacji.

q: Which statements about activating an SKU with `ActivateIfPossible` are correct?
o: `ActivateIfPossible: true` activates the SKU once it has an image or active component
Activating the SKU in the create request returns `400 Bad Request`
`ActivateIfPossible: true` activates the SKU at once, even with no image
It activates the parent product in every trade policy of the store
It enables the SKU price in every price table of the account
`ActivateIfPossible: false` still activates the SKU automatically once an image is added
e: `ActivateIfPossible: true` oznacza **automatyczną aktywację, gdy SKU spełni wymagania** (np. po dodaniu obrazka). Samo tworzenie zawsze z `IsActive: false`, inaczej **400**.

q: How does VTEX distinguish a Product from an SKU?
o: A product is abstract; an SKU is the concrete variation in stock
A product is held in stock; an SKU is only a search keyword
A product belongs to a seller; an SKU belongs to the marketplace
A product is always a kit; an SKU is always a single item
A product holds the price; an SKU holds only the specifications
A product is the item in stock; an SKU groups several products
e: **Produkt** to abstrakcyjna jednostka na półce. **SKU** to konkretny wariant (kolor, rozmiar) trzymany w magazynie.

q: Which request creates a product in the Catalog API?
o: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/product`
`PUT /api/catalog_system/pub/products`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit`
`POST /api/checkout/pvt/product`
`POST /api/catalog_system/pvt/products`
`PUT /api/catalog/pvt/product/{productId}`
e: Produkt: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/product`. SKU: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit`. Zapisz zwrócone `id`.

q: Which request adds an image to an SKU?
o: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/file`
`PUT /api/catalog/pvt/product/{productId}/image`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/sku/{skuId}/media`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/skus/{skuId}/file`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/product/{productId}/file`
`POST /api/catalog_system/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/images`
e: Obrazek to **SKU file**: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/file`.

q: Which statements about trade policies in a product import are correct?
o: The ID of the main trade policy is always 1
Products must be linked to the main trade policy to be displayed in the store
The ID of the main trade policy equals the account name
The main trade policy has ID 0
Trade policies are linked to SKUs through the Pricing API
Products are displayed in every trade policy by default, with no link ever needed
e: Główna trade policy ma zawsze **ID 1**. Produkt musi być do niej przypięty, żeby był widoczny w sklepie. Listę pobierzesz z `GET /api/catalog_system/pvt/saleschannel/list`.

q: Which request links a product to a trade policy?
o: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/product/{productId}/salespolicy/{tradepolicyId}`
`PUT /pricing/tables/{tradepolicyId}/products/{productId}`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/tradepolicy/{tradepolicyId}/sku/{skuId}`
`PATCH /api/checkout/pvt/saleschannel/{tradepolicyId}`
`PUT /api/catalog/pvt/product/{productId}/tradepolicy`
`POST /api/catalog_system/pvt/product/{productId}/salespolicy/{tradepolicyId}/activate`
e: Trade policy przypinasz do **produktu**: `.../product/{productId}/salespolicy/{tradepolicyId}`. `DELETE` na tej samej ścieżce odpina.

q: During a product import, the Catalog API occasionally returns a `Timeout` error. Which statements are correct?
o: A timeout is foreseen within the integration flow
The integration code should envision retries
The import must stop and a new application key must be created
The product must be deleted and the whole import restarted
The same request should be sent to the `/pub/` route instead
A timeout means the account hit its rate limit, so wait 24 hours
e: Timeout jest **przewidziany w przepływie**. Kod integracji ma **ponawiać** żądanie.

q: In the VTEX Catalog, where are specifications registered?
o: On the category, applying to products and SKUs linked to it
On the brand, applying to every product of that brand
On the warehouse, applying to stocked SKUs only
On the trade policy, applying to one sales channel
On the collection, applying to all products and SKUs grouped in it
On the price table, applying to SKUs priced in it
e: Specyfikacje to **właściwości kategorii**. Nadają cechy produktom i SKU z tej kategorii.

q: At least one of which identifiers must an SKU have?
o: `RefId` or `EAN`
`LinkId` or `TaxCode`
`BrandId` or `CategoryId`
`ManufacturerCode` or `Slug`
`Name` or `ProductId`
`MeasurementUnit` or `UnitMultiplier`
e: SKU potrzebuje co najmniej jednego alternatywnego ID: **`RefId` albo `EAN`**.

q: How is the base price of an SKU related to its cost price and markup?
o: `basePrice = costPrice * (1 + markup)`
`basePrice = costPrice + markup`
`basePrice = listPrice * (1 - markup)`
`basePrice = costPrice / (1 - markup)`
`basePrice = costPrice * markup`
`basePrice = listPrice - costPrice * markup`
e: **`basePrice = costPrice * (1 + markup)`**. Gdy podasz dwie wartości, trzecia wylicza się sama.

q: What is a fixed price in VTEX Pricing?
o: A value that overrides the computed price of an SKU in a price table
The suggested retail price shown as the 'from' price
The price left after promotions are applied at checkout
A price that can no longer be changed through the API
The base price that every price table inherits by default from the main table
The cost price recorded for the SKU in the ERP
e: **Fixed price nadpisuje computed price** dla SKU w danej price table / trade policy.

q: Which request creates or updates the base price of an SKU?
o: `PUT /pricing/prices/{itemId}`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/price`
`PATCH /pricing/tables/{itemId}`
`PUT /api/checkout/pvt/prices/{itemId}`
`PUT /api/pricing/pvt/prices/{skuId}/base`
`POST /api/catalog_system/pvt/sku/{skuId}/price`
e: `PUT /pricing/prices/{itemId}` tworzy lub aktualizuje **base price i fixed prices**.

q: Which rate limits does the Pricing API document?
o: `POST` and `PUT` routes: 2000 requests per minute, with 500 burst credits
`DELETE` routes: 1000 requests per minute, with 300 burst credits
`POST` and `PUT` routes: 100 requests per minute, with no burst credits
`DELETE` routes: 5000 requests per minute, with 1000 burst credits
No limit for authenticated application keys
`POST` and `PUT` routes: 500 requests per minute, with 2000 burst credits
e: `POST`/`PUT`: **2000/min (33/s), 500 burst credits**. `DELETE`: **1000/min (16/s), 300 burst credits**.

q: Which statements about Pricing API burst credits are correct?
o: When they reach zero, new requests are blocked with HTTP 429
They refill over time while the route is idle
Requests above the limit are queued and processed later
When they reach zero, the application key is disabled for 24 hours
They are shared by all VTEX APIs of the account
They only apply to `GET` routes of the Pricing API
e: Burst credits = 0 oznacza **429**. Kredyty **odnawiają się, gdy trasa jest bezczynna**. Odczekaj liczbę sekund z nagłówka **`Retry-After`**.

q: What does the computed price represent?
o: The price after applying the price rules of a specific context
The cost price multiplied by the tax rate
The fixed price with the highest minimum quantity
The average of the base price and the list price
The list price minus the active promotions
The base price before any price rule or markup of the table is applied
e: **Computed price** to cena po zastosowaniu reguł cenowych w danym kontekście (price table / trade policy).

q: What is the list price of an SKU?
o: The suggested retail price proposed by the supplier
The price the store paid to acquire the item
The price that overrides all price tables
The price charged for shipping the item
The base price after the markup is applied
The minimum price allowed by the trade policy for the SKU
e: **List price** to sugerowana cena detaliczna, czyli cena pokazywana jako przekreślona.

q: Which strategy do the ERP integration guides recommend for prices when price rules are not used?
o: Send a single base price for each SKU
Set fixed prices as needed to differentiate the value charged for each trade policy
Send a separate base price per trade policy and per warehouse
Send only list prices and let VTEX derive base prices
Send prices inside the Create SKU request body
Send a fixed price for every SKU in every trade policy, even when the values are equal
e: Z ERP idzie **jedna base price na SKU**. Różnice między trade policies ustawiasz przez **fixed prices**.

q: Which base URL is used by the Pricing API?
o: `https://api.vtex.com/{accountName}/pricing`
`https://{accountName}.vtexpayments.com.br/api/pricing`
`https://{accountName}.vtexcommercestable.com.br/api/pricing/pvt`
`https://pricing.vtex.com/{accountName}`
`https://{accountName}.vtexcommercestable.com.br/api/pricing/pub`
`https://portal.vtexcommercestable.com.br/api/pricing/{accountName}`
e: Pricing ma inny host niż reszta: **`api.vtex.com/{accountName}/pricing`**.

q: Your ERP sends stock for an SKU kept in two warehouses. At which level is the stock availability of the SKU stored?
o: Warehouse
Loading dock
Trade policy
Category
Product
Pickup point
e: Stan magazynowy jest trzymany na poziomie **magazynu (warehouse)**. W praktyce: wysyłasz `PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}` osobno dla każdego magazynu.

q: Which request updates the inventory of an SKU?
o: `PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/inventory`
`PATCH /api/logistics/pub/warehouses/{warehouseId}/skus`
`PUT /api/oms/pvt/inventory/{skuId}`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}`
`PUT /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}/stock`
e: Stock to **Logistics API**: `PUT .../inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}`.

q: Which chain describes a logistics route that allows an order to be placed?
o: Warehouse → loading dock → carrier → customer address
Loading dock → warehouse → trade policy → customer address
Carrier → price table → warehouse → customer address
Category → warehouse → pickup point → customer address
Warehouse → carrier → loading dock → customer address
Pickup point → loading dock → warehouse → customer address
e: Trasa: **magazyn → dok → przewoźnik → adres klienta**. Bez pełnej trasy SKU jest niedostępny.

q: What must exist before the inventory of an SKU can be updated?
o: The warehouse that will hold the stock
A fixed price for the SKU
An order that reserves the SKU
A hook configured for inventory events
A price table linked to the warehouse
A collection that includes the SKU
e: Najpierw **utwórz magazyn** (Admin albo `POST /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/warehouses`), potem aktualizuj stock.

q: Which body field of the inventory update sets infinite stock for an SKU?
o: `unlimitedQuantity`
`infiniteStock`
`quantity: -1`
`alwaysAvailable`
`isUnlimited`
`hasUnlimitedStock`
e: Body: `quantity`, **`unlimitedQuantity`** (true = nieskończony stock) i opcjonalnie `dateUtcOnBalanceSystem`.

q: Which statements about the inventory update sent by the ERP are correct?
o: `quantity` carries the total quantity of the SKU in stock
The request is `PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}`
`quantity` carries the difference since the last update
`quantity` carries the quantity already reserved by orders
The request is `POST /api/catalog/pvt/stockkeepingunit/{skuId}/inventory`
The request is `PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/warehouses/{warehouseId}/skus/{skuId}/stock`
e: Wysyłasz **stan całkowity**, nie deltę. Stock to **Logistics API**: `PUT .../inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}`.

q: Which request creates a warehouse programmatically?
o: `POST /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/warehouses`
`PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/warehouses`
`POST /api/catalog/pvt/warehouse`
`POST /api/oms/pvt/configuration/docks`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/docks`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/warehouses/{warehouseId}`
e: Konfiguracja logistyki siedzi pod `/api/logistics/pvt/configuration/...`. Stany są pod `/inventory/...`.

q: When building an orderForm for store pickup, which value is set in `selectedDeliveryChannel`?
o: `pickup-in-point`
`store-pickup`
`delivery`
`pickup`
`pickup-point`
`in-store-pickup`
e: Odbiór w punkcie: `"selectedDeliveryChannel": "pickup-in-point"` w `logisticsInfo`.

q: Your integration keeps a shopping cart through the Checkout API. What is the orderForm it works with?
o: The structure holding all cart data: items, customer, shipping and payment
The invoice document generated after an order ships
The Master Data entity that stores customer addresses
The form used to register a new seller in a marketplace
The temporary token that authenticates the shopper during the checkout
The JSON schema that validates the body of the Place order request before checkout
e: **orderForm** to główny obiekt koszyka: `items`, `clientProfileData`, `shippingData`, `paymentData` i inne. W praktyce: `GET /api/checkout/pub/orderForm` zwraca koszyk z `orderFormId`, którym posługujesz się w kolejnych requestach.

q: Which request simulates a cart to obtain delivery and payment options?
o: `POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForms/simulation`
`GET /api/checkout/pvt/orders/simulate`
`POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/simulation`
`PUT /api/logistics/pvt/shipping/simulation`
`GET /api/checkout/pub/orderForms/simulation`
`POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/simulation`
e: Symulacja koszyka: `POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForms/simulation`. Zwraca `items`, `paymentData`, `logisticsInfo`.

q: Your integration simulates a cart before it places an order. Which data goes in the simulation request body?
o: `items` with `id`, `quantity` and `seller`
`country`
`postalCode` or `geoCoordinates`
The `orderGroup` of the purchase
The payment system ID and the installments
The `transactionId` returned by a previous order
e: Body symulacji: **`items` (id, quantity, seller), `country` (3-literowy ISO), `postalCode` lub `geoCoordinates`**. W praktyce: z odpowiedzi bierzesz `items`, `paymentData` i `logisticsInfo` do budowy orderForm.

q: Which statements about placing an order from a complete orderForm built by the integration are correct?
o: The request is `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders`
A successful request returns `201 Created`
The request is `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders`
A successful request returns `204 No Content`
The request is `PATCH /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}`
A successful request returns `204 No Content` with an empty body
e: Place order to **`PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders`**. Sukces: **`201 Created`**. `204` zwraca dopiero Process order.

q: An order was placed through the Checkout API. Which statements about the next steps are correct?
o: The integration has 5 minutes to send the payment information and process the order
If it does not, the order is automatically canceled
The integration has 30 minutes, the default cancellation window
If it does not, the order stays pending until the user token expires
There is no time limit for this step
If it does not, the order waits for manual approval in the OMS before it is canceled
e: Masz **5 minut** na wysłanie płatności i process order. Potem zamówienie jest **automatycznie anulowane**. 30 minut to okno anulowania w OMS.

q: To which host is the 'Send payments information' request made?
o: `https://{accountName}.vtexpayments.com.br`
`https://{accountName}.vtexcommercestable.com.br`
`https://api.vtex.com/{accountName}`
`https://{accountName}.myvtex.com`
`https://{accountName}.vtexcommercebeta.com.br`
`https://payments.vtex.com/{accountName}`
e: Płatności mają osobny host: `{accountName}.vtexpayments.com.br/api/pub/transactions/{transactionId}/payments`.

q: Which statements about the Process order step are correct?
o: The request is `POST /api/checkout/pub/gatewayCallback/{orderGroup}`
A successful request returns `204 No Content`
The request is `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/start-handling`
A successful request returns `201 Created` with the order in the body
The request is sent to `{accountName}.vtexpayments.com.br`
A successful request returns `202 Accepted` and the order is processed later
e: Process order: `POST /api/checkout/pub/gatewayCallback/{orderGroup}`. Sukces: **`204 No Content`**. Host `vtexpayments.com.br` dotyczy wysłania danych płatności.

q: Your integration placed an order and got an `orderGroup` back. What is the `orderGroup`?
o: An ID that groups all orders created from the same purchase
The ID of the seller that fulfills the order
The trade policy in which the order was placed
The batch of feed events committed together
The ID of the cart the order was placed from, the same as the `orderFormId`
The status group the OMS assigns to orders awaiting payment
e: Jeden zakup od kilku sellerów daje kilka `orderId` (`...-01`, `...-02`) i **jeden `orderGroup`**. W praktyce: `orderGroup` podajesz w `gatewayCallback/{orderGroup}` i jako `orderId` przy wysyłce płatności.

q: What rule applies to data modification requests (`POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) on the Checkout API?
o: They must not be performed in parallel
They must always be sent in batches of ten
They require a user token instead of an appKey
They are accepted only on `/pvt/` routes
They must include the `If-Match` header with the orderForm version
They must be sent with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
e: Modyfikacje koszyka wysyłasz **sekwencyjnie, nigdy równolegle**. Inaczej ryzykujesz uszkodzenie danych.

q: How are monetary values such as an item `price` represented in Checkout API payloads?
o: As integers in cents, so `10000` means 100.00
As decimals with a comma, such as `100,00`
As strings prefixed with the currency code
As floats rounded to four decimal places
As strings with two decimal places, such as `"100.00"`
As integers in thousandths, so `100000` means 100.00
e: Checkout liczy w **centach jako liczby całkowite**: `10000` = 100,00.

q: Place order returned `201 Created`. Which values from the response are needed in the following steps?
o: `transactionId`
`orderGroup`
The `Vtex_CHKO_Auth` cookie
The `X-VTEX-MD-TOKEN` header
The `REST-Content-Range` header
The `X-VTEX-API-AppToken` header
e: Po Place order zachowaj: `transactionId`, `orderId`, `orderGroup`, `addressId` i cookie **`Vtex_CHKO_Auth`**.

q: Why is the Feed recommended over the List orders request for tracking order updates?
o: The Feed runs before indexing and does not depend on it
List orders returns only orders that have already been indexed
The Feed returns the full order details in each event
The Feed has no rate limits for any application key
The Feed returns only the orders of the last 24 hours
List orders returns events in real time, while the Feed is cached for 10 minutes
e: List orders zależy od **indeksowania** (ok. 4 minut opóźnienia). Feed działa **przed indeksowaniem**, więc jest szybszy i pewniejszy.

q: Which statements about Feed and Hook are correct?
o: Feed is a queue: the integration actively retrieves and commits items
Hook sends the items automatically to a URL defined in its configuration
Feed pushes events to a URL; Hook is a queue to pull
Hook handles only payment events
Feed is for sellers; Hook is only for marketplaces
Feed and Hook both require the integration to commit each event it has received
e: **Feed = pull** (sam pobierasz i commitujesz). **Hook = push** (VTEX wysyła na Twój endpoint).

q: Which filter types can be used in a Feed or Hook configuration?
o: `FromWorkflow`
`FromOrders`
`FromStatus`
`FromPayload`
`FromCheckout`
`FromSeller`
e: **`FromWorkflow`** filtruje po statusach. **`FromOrders`** filtruje po dowolnym polu zamówienia wyrażeniem JSONata.

q: A feed is configured with `type: FromWorkflow` and also an `expression` field. What is the response?
o: `409 Conflict`
`200 OK`, and the expression is ignored
`400 Bad Request` caused by a failed ping
`201 Created`, with both filters active
`422 Unprocessable Entity`
`200 OK`, and the status filter is ignored
e: Typy filtrów **wzajemnie się wykluczają**. Mieszanka pól zwraca **409 Conflict**.

q: Which statements about appKeys and order notifications are correct?
o: Each appKey can configure or access only one feed
Each appKey can configure or access only one hook
An appKey can configure one feed per trade policy
An appKey can configure up to ten feeds
An appKey can configure an unlimited number of hooks
An appKey can configure one hook per seller
e: **Jeden feed i jeden hook na appKey.** Użytkownicy dzielący klucz dzielą tę samą kolejkę.

q: Which requests belong to the Feed v3 flow?
o: `GET /api/orders/feed` retrieves feed items
`POST /api/orders/feed` commits feed items
`POST /api/orders/feed/config` saves the feed configuration
`DELETE /api/oms/pvt/feed` commits feed items after reading them
`POST /api/orders/hook/commit` commits feed items after reading them
`PUT /api/orders/feed/config` saves the feed configuration
e: Pobranie: `GET /api/orders/feed`. Commit: `POST /api/orders/feed` z listą `handles`. Konfiguracja: `POST /api/orders/feed/config`.

q: What does `visibilityTimeoutInSeconds` control?
o: How long retrieved items stay hidden before returning to the feed if not committed
How long an item is kept before being deleted from the feed
How long the hook waits for the endpoint to respond
How long an order stays in the cancellation window
How long VTEX waits before it retries a failed feed commit request
How long the feed waits before it sends a retrieved item again to the configured hook endpoint
e: Po pobraniu zdarzenia są **ukryte** przez ten czas. Bez commita **wracają do kolejki**.

q: Which limits apply to `messageRetentionPeriodInSeconds` in the feed configuration?
o: The minimum is 345600 (4 days)
The maximum is 1209600 (14 days)
The minimum is 60 (1 minute)
The maximum is 604800 (7 days)
The maximum is 345600 (4 days)
The minimum is 3600 (1 hour) of retention
e: Retencja: **345600–1209600 s (4–14 dni)**. Po tym czasie zdarzenie znika, nawet bez commita.

q: How must the endpoint configured in a Hook respond to notifications?
o: The expected status is HTTP 200
The time limit is 5000 ms
The expected status is HTTP 202
The time limit is 2.5 seconds
The response body must contain the order ID
The endpoint must answer within 30 seconds
e: Endpoint hooka zawsze odpowiada **HTTP 200 w ciągu 5000 ms**. 2,5 s to limit Fulfillment Simulation sellera.

q: Which statements about configuring a Hook are correct?
o: VTEX sends a `POST` with `{"hookConfig": "ping"}` to the endpoint
If the endpoint does not return 200, the Hook API responds with `400 Bad Request`
VTEX sends a `GET` health check, which must return 204
A sample order JSON is sent and must be echoed back
Nothing is sent; validation happens on the first real event
If the endpoint does not return 200, the hook is saved but stays disabled until resumed
e: Przy konfiguracji idzie **ping**. Brak odpowiedzi 200 oznacza **400 Bad Request** i konfiguracja się nie zapisze.

q: What happens to a Hook that has no notifications for three days?
o: Its configuration is removed and must be created again
It is paused and resumes on the next order
Its events are redirected to the Feed
Nothing; hook configurations never expire
It keeps its configuration but sends a new ping before the next event
It is automatically converted to a feed for the same appKey
e: **3 dni bez powiadomień = konfiguracja hooka usunięta.** Uważaj na zbyt wąski filtr.

q: What must a feed consumer be prepared for regarding the events it receives?
o: Duplicate events and no guaranteed ordering
Events that contain the full order document
Events delivered exactly once and in order
Events that expire after 5000 ms
Events sorted by order creation date
Events that only arrive for orders created through Checkout
e: Feed gwarantuje dostarczenie, ale **nie gwarantuje unikalności ani kolejności**. Middleware musi być idempotentny.

q: The order details were sent to the ERP. Which statements about the next step are correct?
o: The request is `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/start-handling`
It should be done only once per order
The request is `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice`
The request is `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders/{orderId}/handle`
It must be repeated after every feed commit
It is needed only for orders paid with a credit card or a gift card
e: Po przekazaniu do ERP: **`start-handling`**, wywołane **tylko raz** na zamówienie.

q: Which request notifies VTEX that an order was invoiced?
o: `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice`
`PUT /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/status/invoiced`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice`
`PATCH /api/checkout/pub/orders/{orderId}/invoice`
`POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoiced`
`POST /api/orders/pvt/document/{orderId}/invoice`
e: Order Invoice Notification: `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice`. Tracking może dojść później.

q: Which statements about the invoice `type` field are correct?
o: `Output` identifies a selling order invoice
`Input` identifies a return invoice
`Return` identifies a return invoice
`Refund` identifies a return invoice
`Input` identifies the first invoice of an order
`Output` identifies a return invoice
e: **`Output`** to zwykła faktura sprzedaży. **`Input`** to faktura zwrotna.

q: The tracking number becomes available after the order was invoiced. Which request adds it to the existing invoice?
o: `PATCH /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice/{invoiceNumber}`
`POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/tracking`
`PUT /api/logistics/pvt/shipping/{orderId}/tracking`
`POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/start-handling`
`PATCH /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/tracking/{trackingNumber}`
`PUT /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice/{invoiceNumber}/trackingNumber`
e: Tracking jest przypięty do **faktury**: `PATCH .../invoice/{invoiceNumber}`. Statusy przesyłki: `PUT .../invoice/{invoiceNumber}/tracking`.

q: For a typical ERP integration that uses `FromWorkflow`, which order status is the most important to monitor?
o: `ready-for-handling`
`payment-pending`
`order-created`
`invoiced`
`handling`
`window-to-cancel`, then `invoiced`
e: **`ready-for-handling`** oznacza: zapłacone, okno anulowania minęło, można pakować.

q: Why should every feed event be committed, even when no action is taken?
o: Uncommitted events block the integration from receiving the next ones
Uncommitted events cancel the related order
Committing is what changes the order status in the OMS
Committing renews the application token
Uncommitted events are counted against the rate limit of the appKey
Uncommitted events are resent to the hook endpoint every five minutes
e: **Commituj każde zdarzenie.** Niezacommitowane blokują odbiór kolejnych.

q: Which statements about `disableSingleFire` in a `FromOrders` filter are correct?
o: `false`: an order appears in the feed only once after meeting the filter
`true`: an order may appear more than once in the feed
`false` disables the filter, so all orders appear
`true` converts the feed into a hook
`false`: an order appears every time its JSON document changes
`true`: the feed sends only the first status change of the order, then stops
e: `false` = zamówienie trafia do feedu **tylko raz**. `true` może dać wiele zdarzeń dla jednego zamówienia.

q: An ERP calls Cancel order for an order that is already invoiced. What applies according to the OMS order flow?
o: The flow does not allow canceling an order after it is invoiced
The order is canceled and the invoice is deleted
The order goes back to `ready-for-handling`
The cancellation is held for 30 minutes and then applied
The order is canceled and a return invoice is created automatically
The cancellation is accepted only if no tracking number was sent
e: OMS **nie pozwala anulować po zafakturowaniu**, a anulowania nie da się cofnąć. Zwrot wymaga faktury zwrotnej (`type: Input`).

q: How is the Payment Provider Protocol organized?
o: It consists of nine endpoints
The endpoints are divided into Payment Flow and Configuration Flow
It consists of three endpoints: Authorize, Capture and Refund
The endpoints are divided into Seller and Marketplace calls
It is a single webhook that receives all payment events
e: PPP to **9 endpointów**: **Payment Flow** (6) i **Configuration Flow** (3).

q: What does the manifest returned by the provider's `GET /manifest` contain?
o: The supported payment methods
The split configuration
The custom fields
The transactions waiting for settlement
The anti-fraud score of the current transaction
e: **Manifest** to metadane providera: `paymentMethods`, konfiguracja splitu (`allowsSplit`), custom fields.

q: Which status values can a provider return in the Create Payment response?
o: `approved`
`denied`
`undefined`
`pending`
`captured`
e: Trzy statusy: **`approved`**, **`denied`**, **`undefined`** (jeszcze w ocenie).

q: A provider answers Create Payment with `status: undefined`. Which statements are correct?
o: The Gateway retries the call asynchronously for up to seven days
The provider can change the payment status through the `callbackUrl`
The order is canceled after five minutes
The payment is approved after `delayToAutoSettle`
The Gateway retries only once, after 24 hours
e: `undefined` = Gateway **ponawia asynchronicznie do 7 dni**. Provider może też powiadomić przez **`callbackUrl`**.

q: Which field guarantees idempotency in the Cancel, Capture and Refund requests?
o: `requestId`
`transactionId`
`nsu`
`authorizationId`
e: **`requestId`** zapewnia idempotencję: to samo żądanie wysłane wiele razy daje ten sam wynik.

q: Which statements about `delayToAutoSettle` are correct?
o: It defines how long the system waits before starting the settlement flow automatically
It is defined by the provider and specified in seconds
It defines the minutes the shopper has to finish a redirect payment
It defines the days the gateway keeps retrying an undefined payment
It is defined by the merchant in the Admin and specified in days
e: `delayToAutoSettle` i `delayToCancel` ustawia **provider, w sekundach**. Po upływie startuje settlement albo anulowanie.

q: Which are requirements for a payment provider middleware endpoint?
o: Served over HTTPS on port 443 with TLS 1.2
Reached through a domain name, not an IP address
Publicly accessible from the internet
Restricted to the VTEX IP ranges only
Served over HTTPS on port 8443 with TLS 1.2
e: **HTTPS, port 443, TLS 1.2, domena (nie IP), publicznie dostępny.**

q: Which request does VTEX send to capture (settle) a payment?
o: `POST /payments/{paymentId}/settlements`
`PUT /payments/{paymentId}/capture`
`POST /transactions/{transactionId}/settle`
`POST /payments/{paymentId}/refunds`
e: Capture: `/settlements`. Anulowanie: `/cancellations`. Zwrot: `/refunds`. Wszystkie `POST` pod `/payments/{paymentId}/`.

q: An order with an approved payment is canceled. Which statements about the request sent to the provider are correct?
o: If the payment was already settled, the provider receives a refund request
If the payment was not yet settled, the provider receives a cancellation request
In both cases the provider receives a new Create Payment with a negative value
If the payment was already settled, the provider receives a cancellation request
In both cases the provider receives an Inbound Request
e: **Rozliczona** płatność → **refund**. **Autoryzowana, nierozliczona** → **cancellation**.

q: What is true about the PPP Configuration Flow?
o: It is optional for the provider
It yields `appKey`, `appToken` and `applicationId`
It is mandatory and runs before every payment
It replaces the manifest endpoint of the provider
It is used only by anti-fraud providers, not payment ones
e: Configuration Flow jest **opcjonalny**. Daje `appKey`, `appToken`, `applicationId`.

q: How is pagination defined in the Master Data search endpoint?
o: With the `REST-Range` request header
In the format `resources={x}-{y}`, for example `resources=0-100`
With the `_page` and `_pageSize` query parameters
With the `X-VTEX-MD-TOKEN` header
With the `Range: bytes=0-100` header
e: Search stronicujesz nagłówkiem **`REST-Range: resources={x}-{y}`**. Następna strona: `resources=100-200`.

q: What is the maximum number of documents returned by one search request?
e: Search zwraca max **100 dokumentów na żądanie**. Scroll zwraca do 1000.

q: How many documents in total can be retrieved by paginating the search endpoint?
o: Up to 10,000
Up to 1,000
There is no limit
e: Search kończy się na **10 000 dokumentów**. Powyżej tego używasz scrolla.

q: Which statements about the Master Data scroll endpoint are correct?
o: It is for querying the whole database or over 10,000 documents
It returns up to 1000 documents per request
It caps each page at 100 documents, the same as search
It paginates with the `REST-Range` header, like search
Its token never expires, so a scroll can resume later
e: **Scroll** służy do pobierania całej bazy: do **1000** dokumentów na żądanie, token w `X-VTEX-MD-TOKEN` ważny 20 minut. Limit 100 i `REST-Range` dotyczą search.

q: In Master Data scroll requests, which statements about the token are correct?
o: It is returned in the `X-VTEX-MD-TOKEN` response header of the first request
It expires after 20 minutes
It is returned in the `nextToken` field of the response body
It is valid for 24 hours
It is sent back in the `REST-Range` header
e: Token przychodzi w nagłówku **`X-VTEX-MD-TOKEN`**. Podajesz go jako `_token`. Wygasa po **20 minutach**.

q: Which Master Data version supports JSON Schemas?
o: Only Master Data v2
Only Master Data v1
Both v1 and v2
Neither; schemas belong to the Catalog
e: **JSON Schema działa tylko w Master Data v2.**

q: A document is saved in Master Data v2 with a schema. Which statements are correct?
o: It is validated when `_schema={schemaName}` is added to the request
Invalid documents are rejected with HTTP status 400
The schema is chosen by the data entity, so no parameter is needed
The schema is selected with the `X-VTEX-Schema` request header
The document ID must be named after its schema
e: Dodajesz **`?_schema={nazwa}`**. Dokument niezgodny ze schematem wraca z **400**. Bez schematu walidowane jest tylko `id`.

q: Which response header shows the range returned and the total number of matching documents in a search?
o: `REST-Content-Range`
`REST-Range`
`X-Total-Count`
`Content-Length`
e: Odpowiedź: **`REST-Content-Range: resources=0-100/250`**. Żądanie: `REST-Range`.

q: Why is the `_sort` parameter recommended when paginating search results?
o: Without it the order is not guaranteed, which may cause duplicates
Without it the API returns only the first 10 documents
Without it the request is rejected with 400
Without it documents are returned without their `id`
e: Bez **`_sort`** kolejność nie jest gwarantowana. Skutek: duplikaty i nieoczekiwane strony.

q: In a Master Data v2 data entity that has no schema, which fields can be used for searching?
o: `id`
`createdIn`
`updatedIn`
`email`
Every field that holds a numeric value
e: Bez schematu przeszukasz tylko pola wewnętrzne: **`id`, `createdIn`, `updatedIn`**. Schemat włącza kolejne pola.

q: In an external seller integration, which statements about Fulfillment Simulation are correct?
o: The seller implements the endpoint
VTEX marketplaces wait at most 2.5 seconds for the response
The marketplace implements the endpoint and the seller calls it
The caller waits at most 20 seconds for the response
VTEX hosts the endpoint and there is no response time limit
e: Fulfillment Simulation implementuje **seller**. Marketplace czeka max **2,5 s**, potem uznaje produkt za niedostępny.

q: The seller calls Change Notification. Which statements about the response are correct?
o: `404 Not Found` means the SKU does not exist in the marketplace yet
`200 OK` means the SKU already exists in the marketplace
`404 Not Found` means the seller is not registered in the marketplace
After a `404` the seller should call Fulfillment Simulation
`200 OK` means the new price was saved
e: **404** = SKU nie ma w marketplace → wyślij **SKU suggestion**. **200** = SKU istnieje → aktualizuj.

q: What is true about an SKU suggestion sent by a seller?
o: It must be approved by the marketplace to become a registered SKU
After approval, the SKU registration can only be edited by the marketplace
It is published automatically in the marketplace catalog
It can still be edited by the seller after approval
It replaces the price and inventory notifications
e: Katalog należy do **marketplace**. Suggestion wymaga **akceptacji**. Po akceptacji edytuje już tylko marketplace.

q: The payment of a marketplace order is approved. Which statements about Authorize Fulfillment are correct?
o: The marketplace sends the request to the seller
The request body contains only the `marketplaceOrderId`
The seller sends the request to the marketplace
The request body contains the full cart
It is sent before the payment is approved
e: Po zatwierdzeniu płatności **marketplace → seller**: Authorize Fulfillment (`POST /pvt/orders/{sellerOrderId}/fulfill`), w body samo `marketplaceOrderId`.

q: The seller notifies the marketplace about a price or inventory change. What happens next?
o: The marketplace calls the seller's Fulfillment Simulation to fetch the updated data
The marketplace reads the new value from the notification body
The seller must send the SKU suggestion again
The marketplace waits for the next placed order to refresh the data
e: Powiadomienie to tylko sygnał. **Marketplace sam pobiera** aktualne dane przez **Fulfillment Simulation**.

q: Which endpoint must the seller implement to receive new orders from the marketplace?
o: Order Placement (`POST /pvt/orders`)
Place order (`PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders`)
Start handling (`POST .../start-handling`)
Send SKU Suggestion (`PUT`)
e: Seller wystawia **Order Placement** (`POST /pvt/orders`). Marketplace wysyła tam koszyk, klienta, dostawę i płatność.

q: A seller needs to cancel an order that is already in the `Invoiced` status. Which statements are correct?
o: A return invoice must be sent before the cancellation request
The return invoice uses the value `input` in the `type` field
Authorize Fulfillment must be called again first
The related feed event must be committed first
The original invoice must be deleted through the API first
e: Najpierw **faktura zwrotna** (`type: Input`) przez Order Invoice Notification, dopiero potem Cancel Order.

q: Which field indicates that the external seller, not the marketplace, processes the payment?
o: `merchantName`, filled with the seller's account name
`affiliateId`, filled with the marketplace ID
`paymentSystem`, set to zero
`isCheckedIn`, set to true
e: **`merchantName`** z nazwą konta sellera potwierdza, że płatność obsługuje seller.

q: A `POST` request to a VTEX API returns `400 Bad Request`. According to the VTEX status code guide, which causes fit this status?
o: Malformed syntax in the request body
An incorrect `Content-Type` header
Missing or incorrect authentication credentials
The API key has no role with the required resource
The HTTP method is not supported by the endpoint
The requested resource does not exist
e: **400** = serwer nie umiał zdekodować body: **zła składnia** albo **zły `Content-Type`**. Brak danych logowania to **401**, brak roli to **403**, zła metoda to **405**.

q: A request returns `405 Method Not Allowed`. What should the integration check first?
o: Whether the HTTP method matches the documented one
Whether the appToken has expired or was revoked
Whether the account exceeded its request rate limit
Whether the endpoint path is spelled correctly
Whether the request body is valid JSON
Whether the key has a role with the required resource
e: **405** = zła metoda HTTP, np. `POST` zamiast `PUT`. Sprawdź metodę w API Reference. Literówka w ścieżce dałaby **404**, przekroczony limit **429**.

q: A seller calls the price change notification endpoint of a marketplace and receives `202`. What does this status mean?
o: The request was received, but its processing is not completed yet
A new resource was created
The request was processed and there is no content to return
The request was rejected and must be sent again
The request was redirected to another URL
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource and was refused
e: **202 Accepted** = przyjęte, przetwarzanie trwa. **201** = utworzono zasób. **204** = sukces bez treści, np. Start handling.

q: An integration calls `PATCH /api/vtexid/apikey/{apiKey}/apitoken/renew`. Which statements are correct?
o: The old and the new token both work until the renewal is completed
`PATCH .../apitoken/finish-renewal` deactivates the old token
The old token is revoked as soon as the request returns
The new token only becomes active 24 hours after the request
Both tokens stop working until an admin approves the renewal
The renewal also generates a new appKey that replaces the current one
e: Rotacja bez przestoju: **renew** tworzy nowy token i **oba działają**. Dopiero `PATCH .../apitoken/finish-renewal` wyłącza stary. Wymagany resource: **Renew API Token**.

q: Which protocols does VTEX ID use for single sign-on integrations?
o: SAML 2.0 for the Admin
OAuth 2.0 for the Webstore
OAuth 2.0 for the Admin
SAML 2.0 for the Webstore
LDAP for the Webstore
Kerberos 5 for the Webstore
e: **Admin = SAML 2.0**, **Webstore = OAuth 2.0**. Oba konteksty (audiences) obsługuje VTEX ID.

q: Which default rate limits apply to the Catalog API?
o: 45,000 requests per minute per account
15,000 requests per minute per endpoint
2,000 requests per minute with 500 burst credits
5,000 requests per minute per application key
None, because catalog routes are cached
500 requests per minute per IP address
e: Catalog: **45 000/min na konto** i **15 000/min na endpoint**. „2000/min + 500 burst credits” to limit zapisu w **Pricing**.

q: In which order must specifications be created in the Catalog?
o: Specification groups → specification fields → specification values
Specification fields → specification groups → specification values
Specification values → specification fields → specification groups
Specification fields → specification values → specification groups
Specification groups → specification values → specification fields
Specification values → specification groups → specification fields
e: **Grupa → pole → wartość.** Każde pole musi należeć do grupy. Grupy tworzysz od departamentu w dół, bo dziedziczą je kategorie podrzędne.

q: Which specification field types require specification values?
o: `Combo`
`Radio`
`Checkbox`
`Text`
`Number`
`Multi-Line Text`
e: Typy wyliczeniowe to **Combo, Radio, Checkbox**. Dla nich wartości są obowiązkowe.

q: In the Create specification field request, which statements about `IsStockKeepingUnit` are correct?
o: `true` adds the field as an SKU specification
`false` adds the field as a product specification
`true` makes the field mandatory to activate the SKU
`true` shows the field as a filter in search results
`false` copies the field to every SKU of the category
`false` hides the field from the product page
e: `IsStockKeepingUnit: true` = specyfikacja **SKU**. `false` = specyfikacja **produktu**. Obowiązkowość ustawia osobne pole `IsRequired`.

q: `POST /api/catalog/pvt/product` can also create a new category path and a new brand in the same request. Which body fields enable this?
o: `CategoryPath`
`BrandName`
`CategoryId`
`BrandId`
`DepartmentId`
`CategoryName`
e: **Typ 1:** `CategoryPath` + `BrandName` tworzy też kategorie i markę. **Typ 2:** istniejące `CategoryId` + `BrandId`.

q: `GET /api/catalog_system/pvt/products/GetProductAndSkuIds` paginates with `_from` and `_to`. What is the maximum number of records per response?
e: Maks. **250 rekordów**: różnica między `_to` a `_from` nie może przekroczyć 250. Nie myl z Search API, gdzie limit to **50**.

q: The ERP's category structure is not suited for e-commerce. Which statements match the integration guide?
o: Create an inactive mock category (for example, Integration) and import the products into it
The products can later be arranged into the categories appropriate for the store
Send the products without a `CategoryId` and let VTEX classify them
Create one active category for each product
Postpone the product import until the ERP is restructured
Import the products into the main trade policy only, and assign no category to any of them at all
e: Tworzysz **nieaktywną kategorię-atrapę** (np. „Integration”) i wrzucasz tam wszystko. Potem zespół przenosi produkty do właściwych kategorii. Nieaktywna = nic niegotowego nie trafi na sklep.

q: Which limits apply to `GET /api/catalog_system/pub/products/search`?
o: At most 50 items are returned per response
`_from` must be 2500 or lower
At most 250 records are returned per response
Pagination uses the `REST-Range` header
At most 100 items per page, set with `per_page`
e: Maks. **50 produktów** na odpowiedź, sterujesz przez `_from` i `_to`. Dodatkowo `_from` musi być **≤ 2500**. 250 to limit `GetProductAndSkuIds`, `REST-Range` to Master Data, `per_page` to List orders.

q: Which query strings are valid filters of the legacy Search API?
o: `fq=C:/1000041/1000049/` filters by category
`ft=television` filters by full text
`fq=categoryId:1000041` filters by category
`_where=categoryId=1000041` filters by category
`ft=C:/1000041/1000049/` filters by category
e: `fq=C:/{id}/{id}/` = kategoria. `ft=` to **pełny tekst**. Dalej: `fq=productId:`, `fq=skuId:`. `_where` należy do Master Data.

q: How are legacy Search API results sorted by ascending price?
o: `O=OrderByPriceASC`
`_sort=price ASC`
`orderBy=price,asc`
`sort=price:asc`
e: Search API sortuje parametrem **`O`**: `OrderByPriceASC`, `OrderByTopSaleDESC`, `OrderByNameASC`. `_sort=pole ASC` to **Master Data**, `orderBy=pole,asc` to **List orders**.

q: A new headless storefront needs product search. Which API does the documentation require for new headless integrations?
o: Intelligent Search API v1
The legacy Search API (`catalog_system/pub/products/search`)
The Catalog API
The Master Data search endpoint
e: Nowe integracje headless: **Intelligent Search API v1**. Poprzednie Intelligent Search API ma zostać wycofane, a Search API nosi etykietę Legacy.

q: Which cookies does the Sessions System use to identify a session and its commercial context?
o: `vtex_session`
`vtex_segment`
`VtexIdclientAutCookie`
`Vtex_CHKO_Auth`
`checkout.vtex.com`
e: `vtex_session` = sesja konkretnego użytkownika. `vtex_segment` = warunki handlowe (kanał, price tables, region).

q: `POST /api/sessions` is sent with data in several namespaces. Which statements are correct?
o: Only keys in the `public` namespace are stored; the rest is ignored
Query string items are added to `public` automatically
Every namespace sent in the body is stored for the session
Only the `profile` and `store` namespaces are stored
Nothing is stored until the shopper logs in to the store
e: Zapisać możesz tylko **`public`**, np. `country`, `postalCode`, UTM-y. **Query string też trafia do `public`.** Resztę wypełnia platforma.

q: `PUT /pricing/prices/{itemId}` is sent with one fixed price, but the SKU already had three. Which statements are correct?
o: Only the fixed price sent remains; the others are deleted
The body must contain exactly two of `basePrice`, `costPrice` and `markup`
The fixed price is added to the three existing ones
The request fails with `409 Conflict`
Fixed prices are ignored; only the base price changes
The request fails with `400 Bad Request` unless all three fixed prices are sent again
e: Ten **PUT nadpisuje wszystkie fixed prices** SKU. Czego nie ma w body, znika. Podajesz **dokładnie dwie z trzech** wartości `basePrice`, `costPrice`, `markup`; trzy naraz = błąd.

q: Which fields are required in each object of the `fixedPrices` array?
o: `tradePolicyId`
`value`
`minQuantity`
`dateRange`
`listPrice`
`priceTableName`
e: Wymagane: **`tradePolicyId`**, **`value`**, **`minQuantity`**. Opcjonalne: `listPrice` oraz `dateRange` dla cen zaplanowanych.

q: Which statements about the computed price are correct?
o: `GET /pricing/prices/{itemId}/computed/{priceTableId}` returns it
It is the price after every step of the Pricing pipeline
`GET /pricing/pipeline/catalog/{priceTableId}` returns it
It is the cost price multiplied by the account's tax rate
It is the value sent in `listPrice` for the trade policy
`GET /pricing/prices/{itemId}` returns it for every price table at once
e: **Computed price** = cena po całym pipeline. `/pipeline/catalog/...` zwraca **reguły** tabeli, a `listPrice` to sugerowana cena detaliczna.

q: What does `PUT /pricing/pipeline/catalog/{priceTableId}` do with the rules of a price table?
o: Replaces all rules of the table with the ones sent
Appends the rules sent to the table's existing rules
Updates only the rules whose `id` matches one sent
Creates a new price table that holds the rules sent
Deletes the price table together with its prices
Merges the rules by `name` and keeps the rules not sent
e: Zastępuje **cały zestaw reguł**: usuwa stare i tworzy nowe z pola `rules`. Samą tabelę tworzysz przez `PUT /pricing/tables/{priceTableId}`.

q: An integration works with `POST /api/rnb/pvt/coupon`. Which statements are correct?
o: A changed `couponCode` creates a new coupon instead of updating one
The same request both creates and updates coupons
Changing the `couponCode` renames the existing coupon in place
Changing the `couponCode` returns `400 Bad Request`
Changing the `couponCode` archives the existing coupon
It only updates coupons; creating one needs `POST /api/rnb/pvt/multiple-coupons`
e: Kupon identyfikuje **`couponCode`**. Ten sam POST tworzy i aktualizuje. Aktualizacja: pobierz `GET /api/rnb/pvt/coupon/{couponCode}`, zmień body i odeślij całość z **tym samym kodem**.

q: Which request creates a promotion and also updates an existing one?
o: `POST /api/rnb/pvt/calculatorconfiguration`
`PUT /api/rnb/pvt/benefits/calculatorconfiguration/{id}`
`POST /api/rnb/pvt/promotions`
`PATCH /api/rnb/pvt/calculatorconfiguration/{id}`
`PUT /api/rnb/pvt/calculatorconfiguration`
`POST /api/rnb/pvt/benefits/promotion`
e: Jeden endpoint tworzy i aktualizuje promocje **oraz podatki**. Przy aktualizacji wysyłasz w body `idCalculatorConfiguration` i `name`. Archiwizacja: `POST /api/rnb/pvt/archive/calculatorConfiguration/{id}`.

q: Which Logistics API requests update a single inventory attribute (only the quantity or only the lead time) of an SKU in a warehouse?
o: `PATCH /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}/quantity`
`PATCH /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}/lead-time`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/skus/{skuId}/quantity`
`PATCH /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/items/{skuId}/quantity`
`PUT /api/logistics/pvt/inventory/warehouses/{warehouseId}/skus/{skuId}`
`PATCH /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/warehouses/{warehouseId}/skus/{skuId}/quantity`
e: `PATCH .../quantity` zmienia **tylko ilość** (sukces = **204**). `PATCH .../lead-time` zmienia tylko lead time. `PUT` bez sufiksu ustawia oba naraz.

q: `PUT .../inventory/skus/{skuId}/warehouses/{warehouseId}` is sent with `quantity: 10` and `unlimitedQuantity: true`, without `leadTime`. Which statements are correct?
o: The SKU is always available; `unlimitedQuantity` overrules `quantity`
The lead time of the SKU is set to 0
Exactly 10 units are available
The request fails, because the fields are mutually exclusive
10 units are reserved and the rest is unlimited
`unlimitedQuantity` is ignored, because `quantity` is above zero and wins
e: `unlimitedQuantity: true` **wygrywa z `quantity`**. Ten PUT ustawia też lead time: **bez pola `leadTime` lead time spada do 0**.

q: In the inventory of an SKU in a warehouse, what does `leadTime` represent?
o: Handling or manufacturing time before the SKU is ready to ship
The carrier's transit time from the dock to the shopper's address
How long an inventory reservation is held before it expires
The processing time set on the loading dock for outgoing orders
The period after which an SKU is automatically deactivated
The delay before a stock update is reflected in the storefront
e: **Lead time** = czas na poziomie SKU i magazynu (kompletacja, produkcja), zanim towar jest gotowy do wysyłki. Czas doku i czas przewoźnika to osobne ustawienia.

q: Which request creates or updates a pickup point?
o: `PUT /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/pickuppoints/{pickupPointId}`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/pickuppoints`
`POST /api/checkout/pub/pickup-points`
`PUT /api/logistics/pvt/shipping-policies/pickup/{pickupPointId}`
`PATCH /api/logistics/pvt/configuration/pickuppoints/{pickupPointId}`
`POST /api/logistics/pvt/pickup-points/{pickupPointId}`
e: Pickup point: **PUT z ID w ścieżce**, ID bez spacji. Dok i magazyn tworzysz POST-em: `.../configuration/docks` i `.../configuration/warehouses`. `GET /api/checkout/pub/pickup-points` tylko wyszukuje punkty dla klienta.

q: Which statements about `GET /api/checkout/pub/orderForm` are correct?
o: It returns the current cart or creates a new one
`forceNewCart=true` is needed to create a new empty cart
It requires the `orderFormId` as a path parameter
It places the order when `forceNewCart=true` is sent
It only works after `POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForms/simulation`
It returns `404 Not Found` when the session has no cart
e: `GET /api/checkout/pub/orderForm` zwraca bieżący koszyk albo tworzy nowy. **`forceNewCart=true`** wymusza nowy, pusty. Z odpowiedzi bierzesz `orderFormId`.

q: Which statements about adding an SKU to an existing cart are correct?
o: The request is `POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/items`
The body carries an `orderItems` array
The request is `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/items/{skuId}`
The body is sent to `.../attachments/items`
Items should be added in parallel requests to build the cart faster
Each `orderItems` entry must carry the `skuName` of the SKU
e: Każdy element `orderItems`: **`id`** (ID SKU), **`quantity`**, **`seller`**. Modyfikacje koszyka wysyłasz **sekwencyjnie, nigdy równolegle**.

q: `POST .../attachments/shippingData` is sent with an address but without `selectedSla`. Which statements describe what the API does?
o: It selects the option that fulfills the most items for the lowest price
It excludes pickup options and scheduled delivery options
It selects the fastest delivery option available
It always leaves the cart without a delivery option until one is sent
It returns `400 Bad Request`, because `selectedSla` is required
It selects the cheapest option, even if some items in the cart cannot be delivered
e: Bez `selectedSla` API wybiera samo: **najwięcej sztuk za najniższą cenę**. Pomija pickup i dostawy planowane, **nie patrzy na czas dostawy**.

q: Which statements about `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/items/{itemIndex}/price` are correct?
o: It only works when `allowManualPrice` is `true` in the orderForm configuration
The change affects all items in the cart with the same SKU
It requires `canEditData: true` in the orderForm
It requires `allowMultipleDeliveries: true` in the orderForm configuration
It changes the base price of the SKU in Pricing
It works for any item without extra configuration when the request uses an appKey
e: Ręczna cena wymaga **`allowManualPrice: true`** (ustawiasz przez `PATCH /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm`). Zmiana obejmuje **wszystkie pozycje z tym samym SKU** w koszyku.

q: A store needs a new custom field group (`apps`) in every orderForm. Which request registers it?
o: `POST /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm`, after reading the current configuration
`PATCH /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm`, sending only the `apps` array
`PUT /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/customData/{appId}`
`POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/attachments/customData`
`PUT /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm/apps`, sending the new app and its field names
`POST /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm/apps/{appId}`
e: `apps` ustawia tylko **POST** konfiguracji. `PATCH` z polem `apps` zwraca **400 (`CHK0288`)**. POST zapisuje całą konfigurację, więc najpierw zrób `GET` i odeślij komplet. Każdy app ma `id`, `fields`, `major`.

q: Which request sets the value of one custom field in a cart?
o: `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/customData/{appId}/{appFieldName}`
`POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/attachments/openTextField`
`PATCH /api/checkout/pvt/configuration/orderForm`
`POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/customData`
`PATCH /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/customData/{appId}/{appFieldName}`
`POST /api/checkout/pvt/orderForm/{orderFormId}/customFields`
e: **PUT** z `appId` i nazwą pola w ścieżce, wartość w body (`value`). Wiele pól naraz: `PUT .../customData/{appId}`. Wartości trafiają potem do zamówienia w `customData`.

q: The cart already exists as an orderForm. Which statements about placing the order from it are correct?
o: `POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/transaction` places the order
Payment data and processing must follow within five minutes of the order
`POST /api/checkout/pub/gatewayCallback/{orderGroup}` places the order
`POST /api/checkout/pub/orderForm/{orderFormId}/orders` places the order
The order is canceled unless it is invoiced within five minutes of creation
Payment data must be sent within 30 minutes, the default cancellation window of the store
e: Istniejący koszyk: **`POST .../orderForm/{orderFormId}/transaction`**. `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders` składa zamówienie **bez koszyka**. W obu przypadkach masz **5 minut na płatność**.

q: Which limits apply to `GET /api/oms/pvt/orders` (List orders)?
o: Retrieval is limited to 30 pages
15 orders per page by default
Up to 100 orders per page with `per_page`
There is no page limit
Pagination uses the `REST-Range` header
Up to 1000 orders per page with `per_page`
e: **30 stron**, domyślnie **15**, maks. **100** na stronę. Zwraca tylko zamówienia już zaindeksowane (ok. 4 min opóźnienia). Do integracji służy Feed albo Hook.

q: Which sequence shows the fulfillment statuses of an order in the correct order?
o: `window-to-cancel` → `ready-for-handling` → `handling` → `invoiced`
`ready-for-handling` → `window-to-cancel` → `handling` → `invoiced`
`handling` → `ready-for-handling` → `window-to-cancel` → `invoiced`
`window-to-cancel` → `handling` → `ready-for-handling` → `invoiced`
`ready-for-handling` → `handling` → `window-to-cancel` → `invoiced`
`window-to-cancel` → `ready-for-handling` → `invoiced` → `handling`
e: Po zatwierdzeniu płatności: **okno anulowania** → **ready-for-handling** → (Start handling) → **handling** → faktura → **invoiced**. Wcześniej: `payment-pending` → `payment-approved`.

q: By default, how long is the cancellation window in which the customer can cancel an order without store approval?
o: 30 minutes after payment approval
5 minutes after the order is placed
24 hours after payment approval
Until the order is invoiced
15 minutes after the order is placed
7 days after the order is invoiced
e: `window-to-cancel` trwa domyślnie **30 minut** od zatwierdzenia płatności. Sklep może zmienić ten czas w ustawieniach. Nie myl z 5 minutami na płatność w Checkout API.

q: The integration calls `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/start-handling`. Which statements are correct?
o: A successful request returns `204 No Content`
If the response differs from 204, the store must retry the call
A successful request returns `200 OK` with the updated order in the body
A successful request returns `201 Created` with a handling ID
A successful request returns `202 Accepted`; the status changes after the feed is committed
If the response differs from 204, the order is canceled automatically
e: Sukces = **204 bez treści**. Inny kod, np. 500, oznacza **ponów wywołanie** i jest to obowiązek sklepu.

q: Which of these fields are required in the body of the Order invoice notification request?
o: `type`
`issuanceDate`
`invoiceValue`
`trackingNumber`
`courier`
`invoiceUrl`
e: Wymagane: **`type`, `issuanceDate`, `invoiceNumber`, `invoiceValue`, `items`**. Tracking (`courier`, `trackingNumber`, `trackingUrl`) jest opcjonalny i można go dosłać później.

q: Which statements about a return invoice (`type: Input`) are correct?
o: It triggers the refund by itself, with no extra API request
It only refunds if the full order amount was invoiced first
It moves the order status back to `handling` for a new shipment
It cancels the order and restores the stock of its items
Nothing happens until the Refund payment request is called
It requires the `trackingNumber` of the original shipment
e: `Input` **sam uruchamia zwrot pieniędzy**. Warunek: wysyłaj go dopiero wtedy, gdy **cała kwota zamówienia była zafakturowana**, inaczej zwrotu nie będzie.

q: Which statements about `PUT /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/invoice/{invoiceNumber}/tracking` are correct?
o: It sends tracking events for an invoice that already has a tracking number
Its body requires `isDelivered`, `deliveredDate` and `events`
It adds the tracking number and the tracking URL to an invoice
It creates a new invoice together with its tracking data
It replaces the carrier of an invoiced order
Its body requires `trackingNumber`, `trackingUrl` and the `courier` of the invoice
e: To **zdarzenia przesyłki**. Body: `isDelivered`, `deliveredDate`, `events`. Numer i URL śledzenia dodajesz wcześniej przez `PATCH .../invoice/{invoiceNumber}`.

q: Which statements about changing the items or the value of an existing order are correct?
o: `PATCH /api/order-system/orders/{changeOrderId}/changes` is the current request
`POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/changes` is being deprecated
`PUT /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}` replaces the order
`PATCH /api/checkout/pub/orders/{orderId}/items` changes the items
Orders can be changed in any status, including `invoiced`
Changes are allowed only while the order is still in the `window-to-cancel` status
e: **Change v2** = `PATCH /api/order-system/orders/{id}/changes`. `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/changes` to v1, **wycofywane**. Dozwolone statusy: `handling`, `waiting-for-fulfillment`, `ready-for-invoicing`.

q: Which of these orders can still be canceled with `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders/{orderId}/cancel`?
o: An order in `handling` that has no invoice
A partially invoiced order
An order with the `invoiced` status
An incomplete order
An order whose invoice was sent with `type: Output`
An order that already has a tracking number on its invoice
e: Nie anulujesz zamówień **częściowo zafakturowanych** (zamiast tego Change order), **invoiced** (zamiast tego faktura zwrotna `Input`) ani **niekompletnych**. W body podajesz `reason`. Anulowania nie da się cofnąć.

q: In the redirect purchase flow, which statements about the Create Payment response are correct?
o: The provider returns the status `undefined`
The provider returns a `paymentUrl`, to which the shopper is redirected
The provider returns the status `approved` together with a `returnUrl`
The provider returns the status `denied` together with a `callbackUrl`
The provider returns `paymentAppData`
e: **Redirect:** `undefined` + **`paymentUrl`**. `paymentAppData` należy do flow Payment App. `callbackUrl` i `returnUrl` przychodzą **w żądaniu** od VTEX.

q: A provider must show a QR code or a 3D Secure 2 challenge inside the checkout, without leaving the store. Which flow fits?
o: Payment App flow: return `undefined` with `paymentAppData`
Transparent flow: return `approved` with `paymentUrl`
Redirect flow: return `undefined` with `paymentUrl`
Configuration flow: return `applicationId`
e: **Payment App** = aplikacja VTEX IO renderowana w checkoucie. Provider zwraca `undefined` + `paymentAppData` (`appName`, `payload`). Trzy flow zakupowe: **transparent**, **redirect**, **payment app**.

q: A payment returned `undefined`. The connector is external middleware, not built on VTEX IO. How does it report the final status?
o: By sending a notification `POST` to the `callbackUrl` with the updated response
By calling the retry endpoint, so the Gateway sends Create Payment again
By calling `POST /api/pvt/transactions/{transactionId}/authorization-request`
By waiting for the Gateway to poll `GET /payments/{paymentId}`
e: **Poza VTEX IO = Notification**, czyli POST na `callbackUrl`. **Na VTEX IO = Retry**, Gateway ponawia Create Payment. Callback uwierzytelniasz kluczem konta partnera: `X-VTEX-API-AppKey` i `X-VTEX-API-AppToken`.

q: How fast must a payment provider endpoint respond?
o: The limit is 5 seconds when running the tests
The limit is 20 seconds in production
The limit is 2.5 seconds in every environment
The limit is 5000 ms in production
The limit is 45 seconds, the Checkout timeout
e: PPP: **poniżej 5 s w testach** i **poniżej 20 s na produkcji**. Nie myl: 2,5 s to Fulfillment Simulation sellera, 5000 ms to Hook zamówień.

q: Which payment connectors must use the Secure Proxy to accept card payments?
o: Connectors hosted without a PCI DSS certification
All connectors built on VTEX IO
Only connectors that use the redirect payment flow
Every connector, even one with a PCI DSS certification
Only connectors that process gift card payments
e: Secure Proxy jest dla środowisk **bez PCI DSS**, w tym **wszystkich konektorów na VTEX IO**.

q: VTEX calls Create Payment again with a `paymentId` the provider has already processed. What must the provider do?
o: Return the current status of that payment; create nothing new
Create a second payment and cancel the first one afterwards
Respond with `409 Conflict` and the original `paymentId`
Respond with `denied`, because the ID is a duplicate
e: Create Payment jest **idempotentny po `paymentId`**. Provider musi być gotowy na powtórzone żądania i zwracać aktualny status. W Cancel, Capture i Refund idempotencję zapewnia `requestId`.

q: What is true about a gift card created with `POST /giftcards` in the native Giftcard API?
o: It is created with a zero balance
`profileId` is required in the request body
It is created with the value sent in the `balance` field
Its `redemptionCode` must be sent in the request body
It is a promotion that is applied automatically at checkout
e: Przez API: **saldo 0** i obowiązkowy **`profileId`**. Saldo dodajesz transakcją: `POST /giftcards/{id}/transactions`. `redemptionCode` generuje się sam.

q: Which statements about the Anti-fraud Provider Protocol are correct?
o: `POST /transactions` is sent only if all payments of the transaction are authorized
`POST /pre-analysis` is an optional step performed before payment authorization
`POST /transactions` is sent before the payments are sent for authorization
`POST /transactions` is sent only after the order is invoiced
`POST /pre-analysis` is sent only when a payment is denied by the acquirer
e: Pełna analiza idzie **po autoryzacji wszystkich płatności**. Przed autoryzacją działa tylko opcjonalne `POST /pre-analysis`.

q: Which statements about customer data in Master Data are correct?
o: `CL` stores customer profiles
`AD` stores customer addresses
`CU` stores customer profiles
`SH` stores shipping addresses
`CL` and `AD` are Master Data v2 entities
e: **`CL`** = klienci, **`AD`** = adresy, oba w **Master Data v1**. Adres wiążesz z klientem polem `userId`.

q: In the Master Data API, which statements about `/documents/{id}` are correct?
o: `PUT` creates a document with that ID or replaces it whole
`PATCH` updates only the fields sent
`PUT` updates only the fields sent and keeps the rest
`PATCH` replaces the entire document with the body
`PUT` works only in v1 and `PATCH` only in v2
e: **PUT = cały dokument** albo utworzenie z własnym ID. **PATCH = częściowa aktualizacja**, reszta pól zostaje.

q: Which request finds customers whose first name is Jon or whose last name is Smith?
o: `GET /api/dataentities/CL/search?_where=(firstName=Jon OR lastName=Smith)`
`GET /api/dataentities/CL/search?fq=firstName:Jon,lastName:Smith`
`GET /api/dataentities/CL/documents?firstName=Jon&lastName=Smith`
`POST /api/dataentities/CL/search` with a JSONata `expression`
e: Filtry złożone idą w **`_where`**: `OR`, `AND`, `between`, `is null`, `<>`, `>`. Prosty filtr: `?email=a@b.com`. Częściowy: `?firstName=*Maria*`. Zwracane pola wybierasz przez `_fields`.

q: A Master Data v2 search uses `_where` and `_fields` on custom fields. Which parameter is required as well?
o: `_schema`, naming the schema the documents follow
`_keyword`, with the full-text term to match
`_token`, returned by the previous page of results
`_size`, with the number of documents per page
e: W v2 pola własne są przeszukiwalne tylko przez schemat, więc `_where` i `_fields` wymagają **`_schema={nazwa}`**. Nadużywanie wildcardów (`*`) i `keyword` może czasowo zablokować endpoint, dostaniesz **503**.

q: Where is a Master Data v2 trigger defined?
o: In the `v-triggers` array of the data entity's JSON schema
In `POST /api/dataentities/{dataEntityName}/triggers`
In the `hook` field of each document
In the orderForm configuration
e: Trigger to obiekt w **`v-triggers`** schematu: `name`, `active`, `condition`, `action`, opcjonalnie `retry` i `runAt`. Typy akcji: `http`, `email`, `t-email`, `save`. Domyślnie 3 próby co 10 minut.

q: An external marketplace sells the products of a VTEX seller. Which statements about creating the order in the seller's account are correct?
o: The request is `POST /api/fulfillment/pvt/orders`
The `affiliateId` query parameter identifies the marketplace where the order originates
The request is `PUT /api/checkout/pub/orders` with the `sc` query parameter
The request is `POST /pvt/orders` on the seller's fulfillment endpoint
The request is `POST /api/oms/pvt/orders` with the `marketplaceOrderId` in the body
e: **Zewnętrzny marketplace → seller VTEX:** `POST /api/fulfillment/pvt/orders?affiliateId={id}&sc={kanał}`. `POST /pvt/orders` to kierunek odwrotny: marketplace VTEX → zewnętrzny seller.

q: The marketplace with affiliate ID `MKP` placed order `123` in a VTEX seller. Which `orderId` authorizes its dispatch in `POST /api/fulfillment/pvt/orders/{orderId}/fulfill`?
e: `orderId` = **`affiliateId` + `-` + `marketplaceOrderId`**, czyli `MKP-123`. W body idzie samo `marketplaceOrderId` (`123`). Sukces = **201**.

q: A seller calls `POST /api/notificator/{sellerId}/changenotification/{skuId}/price` on a VTEX marketplace. Which statements are correct?
o: The call has no request body
The marketplace then calls the seller's fulfillment endpoint to get the updated price
The body carries the new price in cents
The body carries the price table and the trade policy of the SKU
The body carries the full SKU payload, as in an SKU suggestion
e: Powiadomienie **bez body**. Mówi tylko, że coś się zmieniło. Marketplace sam odpytuje Fulfillment Simulation sellera. Tak samo działa `.../inventory`.

q: In the Place fulfillment order request sent by an external marketplace, how is `paymentData` filled?
o: It is sent as `null`, because the payment is processed by the marketplace
With the card tokens received from the Secure Proxy
With the `transactionId` returned by the Payments Gateway
With the payment system ID chosen by the customer
e: Płatność obsługuje **marketplace**, więc do sellera idzie `paymentData: null`. Wymagane pola: `marketplaceOrderId`, `marketplaceServicesEndpoint`, `marketplacePaymentValue`, `items`, `clientProfileData`, `shippingData`.

q: Which facet is mandatory in the `{facets}` path of the Intelligent Search `product_search` endpoint?
o: `trade-policy`
`category-1`
`brand`
`productClusterIds`
e: Jedyny **wymagany** facet to `trade-policy/{id}`, np. `trade-policy/1`. `category-n`, `brand`, `productClusterIds`, `price` i specyfikacje to opcjonalne filtry. Bez nich dostajesz wszystkie produkty danej polityki handlowej.

q: An Intelligent Search `product_search` request omits `page` and `count`. What does it return?
o: Page 1 with 24 products
Page 0 with 50 products
Page 1 with 50 products
Page 1 with 100 products
